claims.text: Exposure of HfNbTaTiZr to 500–1000 °C modifies its dislocation-core structures.
Exposure of HfNbTaTiZr to 500–1000 °C increases lattice anharmonicity.
Dislocation-core modifications and increased lattice anharmonicity cause a reduction in the elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally enhanced dislocation glide and core restructuring reduce the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr.
Increased anharmonic lattice-vibration amplitudes increase the thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
The baseline as-cast, thermally stabilized HfNbTaTiZr has a primarily single-phase microstructure.
Incremental annealing between 500 and 1000 °C is the proposed intervention.
Mechanical and diffraction testing at 500, 700, and 900 °C can resolve elevated-temperature elastic and stress–strain behavior.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have lower yield strength than the baseline state within 500–1000 °C.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have lower elastic moduli than the baseline state within 500–1000 °C.
Heat-treated HfNbTaTiZr will have a higher coefficient of thermal expansion than the baseline state within 500–1000 °C.
The proposed mechanism should remain applicable up to 1000 °C if significant phase transformation and recrystallization are absent.
Strain-rate variation may affect the measured high-temperature mechanical response.
Microstructural heterogeneity may affect the magnitudes of the yield-strength, modulus, and expansion changes.
Absence of statistically significant strength and modulus reductions or thermal-expansion enhancement would falsify the hypothesis.
